attribute_definitions.label: Item family
attribute_definitions.note: What the item IS. 'grille, type not stated' when the text gives a grille but not its type; 'none of these' for a priceable thing outside the sheet's families (owner ruling 6b: no SKU in the catalogue means the row is left blank for the user to decide). A discrete grille is 'grille, type not stated'. A row that gives only a size, or a size and a place ('600x600 for hub room'), buys the item its heading or that heading's note describes: answer that family, never 'none of these' with the size as its name. A row that buys something returns at least one item: an item outside the list is 'none of these' with 'Item as written' -- never an empty list. ALTERNATIVE NAMES (owner ruling 3a, 2026-09-23): a single skin plenum, a spill air box / spill air plenum, a plenum box, a diffuser box or a mixing chamber is 'mixing box / LP plenum'; 'double-skin plenum' ONLY when the text says double skin / double-skinned. Every louvre (intake, exhaust, discharge, fresh air, non-vision) is 'intake louvre'; a non-vision door louver is 'door grille'; a tegular or plaque diffuser is 'square diffuser'; on a row priced per sq.m, a diffuser whose shape the row and its headings do not settle -- no shape named, or round and square both offered ('round/square') -- is 'square diffuser' (owner 2026-10-23); a spigot damper is 'spigot' (code prices it as the Butterfly Damper With Spigot); a multi-blade louver damper is 'VCD'; a double deflection grille is 'linear grille' (a curved grille stays 'curved grille'); a grille damper is 'collar damper'; a floor tile grille, a rigid floor grille or a rigid tile grille is 'floor grille'. A Z-piece, a Z type baffle, a Z baffle or a cross talk silencer is 'cross-talk' (owner 2026-10-23), also under a heading that names another family (a Z type baffle under an ACTUATORS heading is 'cross-talk'). A return air baffle is 'cross-talk' (owner 2026-10-23); return it alone -- code adds its return air grille. A SECOND ITEM NEEDS WORDS: where nothing in the row or its own ancestors mentions a plenum box, a spill air box or a mixing chamber, a diffuser row pays for the diffuser alone -- do not add a box because diffusers often have one. Where an ancestor does describe the row's item as including one, both items are returned. A PLENUM'S ACCESSORIES ARE PART OF IT (owner 2026-10-23): where the row's item is a 'double-skin plenum' or a 'mixing box / LP plenum' itself, an access door or any other accessory the row names with it (hangers, cut-outs, openings) is not a second item -- return the plenum alone; its rate includes them. A canvas connection is NOT an accessory: where the row says its price includes canvas connections, return 'canvas connection' as a second item beside the plenum (owner 2026-10-23). A DAMPER NAMED AS PART OF A GRILLE OR DIFFUSER IS NOT A SECOND ITEM: a row buying a grille or a diffuser that the text says comes with a collar, volume-control or hit-and-miss damper pays for ONE item -- the grille or diffuser, with its damper attribute set. A damper is its own item only where the row buys the damper itself and names no host. A MOTORISED VCD'S CONTROL PANEL, ACTUATOR AND CABLING named in its heading are not separate items (owner 2026-10-23): return the VCD alone; code says on the panel that they are not included.

attribute_definitions.label: Damper
attribute_definitions.note: Owner default (R1) when 'None': without (curved grille: with). 'None' = the text says nothing about a damper. The ROW WINS over a heading: a row saying it is without a volume control damper is 'without', even where a neighbouring section heading names a damper product. WHERE THE ROW NAMES A DAMPER AS PART OF A GRILLE OR DIFFUSER, that is this item's damper: answer 'with' here and return no separate damper item. Three shapes this covers: a grille described with a collar damper; a curved or linear grille with its damper in the same sentence; a diffuser whose stated size is followed by a damper. Where the row buys dampers alone, the damper IS the item and this attribute describes nothing else.

attribute_definitions.label: Neck size (as written)
attribute_definitions.note: A SQUARE or rectangular item's neck size, as written. A round item's neck is its diameter and belongs in the diameter attribute instead.

attribute_definitions.label: Size (as written)
attribute_definitions.note: The item's OWN size, copied exactly as the row writes it, in ONE field: a face or outer size ("600 x 600"), or a box size with its depth ("525 x 525 x 450 mm"), or a single dimension where that is all the text gives. Keep the whole phrase together, INCLUDING the unit and any word or letter that names a dimension -- (W) / (H) / (D) / (L), 'wide', 'high', 'deep', 'long' -- and keep them in the order the text writes them; code splits the phrase into width, height and depth and reads those labels. A row giving only ONE dimension must keep its word too (a grille that is only '250 mm high' is a height, not a width). It is NOT the neck size and NOT a diameter -- those have their own attributes.

attribute_definitions.label: Diameter (as written)
attribute_definitions.note: The item's diameter as written. On a ROUND item the neck size IS the diameter, however the row words it, so a round item's stated neck belongs here.

attribute_definitions.label: Insulation material
attribute_definitions.note: Which insulation the row buys. The family: it decides the SKU set and the unit. Open cell is Acoustic Nitrile Insulation; closed cell on a duct, sheet, wall, ceiling or slab is Thermal Nitrile Insulation, also where the row or its heading calls it acoustic insulation ('acoustic insulation ... with closed cell nitrile rubber' on a duct is Thermal Nitrile Insulation); closed cell on a pipe is Nitrile Rubber Insulation. Fibre glass, glass wool or resin-bonded glass wool of ANY density -- 32 kg/m3 included -- is ' Fiberglass Rigid Board Insulation, Density 48Kg/m3' (the density is ignored). 'none of these' for an insulation material the catalogue does not stock (rockwool, mineral wool, XLPE, phenolic, EPDM, PIR, polyethylene / EPS). A row that names only a GENERIC insulation -- 'insulation', 'insulation foam', 'foam insulation' -- and no material of its own takes the material its heading names: under a heading naming nitrile rubber it is nitrile (Nitrile Rubber Insulation on a pipe, Thermal Nitrile Insulation on a duct or sheet). 'none of these' is only for a material the catalogue does not stock, never for a generic word. Answer 'none of these' only for a material the BoQ NAMES that the catalogue does not stock; when the row and its headings name no insulation material at all, leave this out -- the pricer applies the ruled default. Where the BoQ offers materials as alternatives ('nitrile rubber/XLPE', 'rockwool/glasswool'), copy the material as written in full, both names, into 'Insulation material as written'. A row that describes only a cladding or coating applied over insulation, with no insulation material being supplied, is 'Cladding Only'. Tubular nitrile rubber, nitrile tube or nitrile tubing (any spelling of nitrile) is Nitrile Rubber Insulation; 'Tubular Puf Insulation' only where PUF or polyurethane is named.

attribute_definitions.label: Cladding
values: GI Framework with perforated Al sheet
attribute_definitions.note: What covers the insulation. 'No' means the row states none. A cladding a heading names applies to every row under it that changes only the material or the thickness and names no cladding of its own: answer the heading's cladding there. A cladding a heading names with 'where required', 'if required', 'as required' or 'as directed' still applies to every row under that heading: answer it. Only a condition that names WHERE the item is (pipes exposed to sun or atmosphere, outdoor, exposed areas) limits the cladding to rows that meet that condition. 'Exposed insulation material with <a cladding>' describes the insulation's own outer face, not a place: that cladding applies to every row under the heading (owner 2026-10-23). Aluminium foil and glass cloth offered as alternatives ('Al Foil / GC cloth') is 'Aluminium Foil'. When neither the row nor its headings mention a cladding, answer 'None' - never leave it out for that reason. 'Al. foil', 'Alu foil' or aluminium foil is 'Aluminium Foil'. A GI or galvanised sheet cladding with no frame and no perforated sheet named ('26 G GI cladding') is not stocked: LEAVE THIS OUT and copy the cladding exactly as written into 'Cladding as written'. A GI frame, grid or framework of any gauge (a 22G GI frame work) carrying a perforated sheet is 'GI Framework with perforated Al sheet'. A perforated GSS sheet (galvanised steel sheet, 22G / 26G, powder coated or not) carried on such a frame is the SAME cladding, 'GI Framework with perforated Al sheet' -- the sheet metal the row names does not make it a different cladding, so do not flag or withhold it for saying GSS rather than aluminium. A paint or coating over glass cloth (two coats of UV paint, a flame-retardant coating sandwiched with glass cloth) is 'Glass Cloth with paint' -- a paint or coating alone NEVER makes it aluminium. A paint or coating ('polyshield coating', 'fire retardant coating', 'protective coating', a UV coating, a lacquer) is not a cladding and never changes the price (owner 2026-10-23): where it is the only covering the text names, with no glass cloth, answer 'None' -- never 'Glass Cloth with paint' -- and leave it out of 'Cladding as written'. A cladding named beside it (an aluminium sheet, a foil) is answered as that cladding. Where the coating IS sandwiched with or applied over glass cloth, it is the paint of 'Glass Cloth with paint': copy the words up to and including the glass cloth into 'Cladding as written'. A co-extruded polymer jacket or covering is copied as written into 'Cladding as written' and never mapped to a stocked cladding. Where aluminium is ALSO named beside the glass cloth it is '<gauge> Aluminium with Glass Cloth' at the gauge the BoQ states; aluminium named with no gauge is 26G ('26G Aluminium', '26G Aluminium with Glass Cloth'): no gauge stated -> priced as 26G. A perforated GSS sheet bolted or screwed on with no frame named is still 'GI Framework with perforated Al sheet'. A bare 'glass cloth' with no paint or coating named is still 'Glass Cloth with paint'. A factory-laminated or reinforced glass cloth or fibre cloth facing ('factory laminated fire resistant fibre cloth fabric', 'reinforced glass cloth') IS the glass cloth cladding: 'Glass Cloth with paint', or '<gauge> Aluminium with Glass Cloth' where aluminium is also named. A FOIL facing ('reinforced foil facing', 'foil facing', 'foil-faced', 'FSK') is 'Aluminium Foil', never a glass cloth (owner 2026-10-23); an aluminium cladding and a foil facing offered as alternatives ('aluminum cladding / reinforced foil facing') is 'Aluminium Foil'.

attribute_definitions.label: Cladding as written
attribute_definitions.note: The cladding in the BoQ's OWN WORDS, copied exactly as the row or its heading writes it ('26 G GI cladding', '24 G aluminium with glass cloth'). Answer it whenever the text names a cladding, also when 'Cladding' is answered; leave it out when no cladding is named. Recorded and shown; the pricer maps a cladding the catalogue does not stock. Copy the words exactly as the BoQ writes them, as one continuous piece; never shorten, never join pieces with '...' or any other mark; if the words are long, copy the shortest continuous piece that holds the value.

attribute_definitions.label: Thickness (mm)
attribute_definitions.note: The insulation thickness AS THE ROW WRITES IT, in mm. Never converted. Read it in this order and stop at the first that applies: (1) the row's OWN value -- a thickness in the row's description or in a note attached to the row -- always wins, even where a heading says otherwise; (2) else, where a heading keys the thickness to the pipe size (a schedule such as '25mm to 50 mm : 19mm thick'), read the thickness for THIS row's pipe size and return that one value; (3) else, where the text lists several thicknesses with no such schedule, copy the list as written; (4) else leave the attribute out. Where the text states two layers ('19 mm x 2', '2 layers of 19 mm', '25 mm thick - 2 Layers'), copy it as written -- never add the layers up. Under a PIPE heading, 'A mm + B mm thick' is the PIPE SIZE and the insulation THICKNESS (65 mm + 32 mm thick = a 65 mm pipe with 32 mm of insulation), not two layers: return B here and A as the pipe size. Copy the words exactly as the BoQ writes them, as one continuous piece; never shorten, never join pieces with '...' or any other mark; if the words are long, copy the shortest continuous piece that holds the value.

attribute_definitions.label: Pipe size (mm)
attribute_definitions.note: The pipe's nominal size AS THE ROW WRITES IT. Pipe families only. Under a pipe heading, 'A mm + B mm thick' names the pipe size first: A is the pipe size, B the insulation thickness. Copy the words exactly as the BoQ writes them, as one continuous piece; never shorten, never join pieces with '...' or any other mark; if the words are long, copy the shortest continuous piece that holds the value.

attribute_definitions.label: Brand
attribute_definitions.note: The make or brand the row names for this item, copied as written. It is recorded and shown; it is never used to choose a catalogue row. Copy the words exactly as the BoQ writes them, as one continuous piece; never shorten, never join pieces with '...' or any other mark; if the words are long, copy the shortest continuous piece that holds the value.

attribute_definitions.label: Insulation material as written
attribute_definitions.note: The insulation material exactly as the row or its heading names it (XLPE, rockwool, nitrile rubber). A co-extruded polymer jacket or covering is copied here as written too. Copied as written; it is what a pricer is told when the catalogue has no SKU for it. Copy the words exactly as the BoQ writes them, as one continuous piece; never shorten, never join pieces with '...' or any other mark; if the words are long, copy the shortest continuous piece that holds the value.

attribute_definitions.label: Coating as written
attribute_definitions.note: A paint or coating the row or its heading names that is NOT the paint of 'Glass Cloth with paint' (a UV coating, a fire or flame retardant coating, a polyshield or protective coating, a lacquer), in the BoQ's own words; leave it out when no such coating is named. Shown on the panel only: the price never reads it. Copy the words exactly as the BoQ writes them, as one continuous piece; never shorten, never join pieces with '...' or any other mark; if the words are long, copy the shortest continuous piece that holds the value.

attribute_definitions.label: Pipe type
attribute_definitions.note: Which pipe THIS row buys - one of the four stocked types. Answer it only when the row's own text, or a heading that describes this row's pipe, names that very type or the service that decides it: copper, refrigerant, VRF or VRV piping is Copper, also where the word copper is not written, and on EVERY pipe row under such a heading, whatever level the heading sits at (a 'VRF SYSTEM' heading two or three levels up still makes each pipe row below it Copper) - unless the row itself, or a nearer heading, names another type for that pipe (a uPVC drain under a VRF heading is uPVC); MS or mild steel piping is MS, and chilled water piping that names no type is MS; PVC is PVC; CPVC is CPVC. A drain or condensate line takes the type the text names for it. A drain pipe whose material the BoQ does not name: leave the pipe type out (do not guess); the code prices it as CPVC. The row's own word wins over a heading: a row that says PVC under a CPVC heading is PVC. Where the text names any other type (GI, uPVC, HDPE, SS, anything else), or names two different types for this pipe and the row itself does not say which, LEAVE THIS OUT - never choose the nearest stocked type; the pricer does that from 'Pipe type as written'. Return one item per pipe the row pays for. Testing, painting, sleeves, welding, nitrogen or vacuum work, civil work, identification and valves named with the pipe are NOT items and change no attribute: ignore them.

attribute_definitions.label: Pipe type as written
attribute_definitions.note: The pipe's type in the BoQ's OWN WORD, copied exactly as written: from the row's own text when it names one, else from the nearest heading that describes this row's pipe (copper, MS, GI, uPVC, HDPE, SS). Answer it on every pipe whose type the text names, also when 'Pipe type' is answered. Where the text names two or more types for this pipe, copy them all as written ('MS / GI', 'uPVC/ CPVC'). Copy the TYPE word when the row or any heading writes one: under 'COPPER REFRIGERANT PIPINGS' it is 'COPPER', never 'Refrigerant'. Only where no type word is written anywhere in the text, write the service word as written ('VRF', 'refrigerant', 'chilled water') or leave this out. Copy only words the text actually writes - never a type the text does not contain. Leave it out when neither the row nor its headings name a type. Recorded and shown; the pricer maps it or refuses it by name. Copy the words exactly as the BoQ writes them, as one continuous piece; never shorten, never join pieces with '...' or any other mark; if the words are long, copy the shortest continuous piece that holds the value.

attribute_definitions.label: Pipe size
attribute_definitions.note: The pipe's own size AS THE ROW WRITES IT, with its unit: mm, an NB number (50 NB), inches (5/8", 1-1/4", 2 inch) or an outside diameter in mm (22.3 mm O.D). Never converted, never rounded. The row's own size comes first; a heading gives the size only when the row states none. Where the text names two sizes and says which one is this pipe's, return that one; otherwise copy both as written (25/32 mm). Where the row writes its size as a bare number with no unit (3/4, 1, 1-1/4), take the UNIT - never the size - from a heading that describes this row's pipe, or from the neighbouring rows of the same list (rows beside it written 3/4", 1", 1-1/4" make a bare 1 an inch size), and write the unit with the size ('1 inch'). Where neither the row, its headings nor its neighbours give a unit, return the number bare, exactly as written. A wall thickness, a gauge, a class, a schedule or a pressure rating is NEVER the pipe size: in '22.3 mm O.D (wall Thickness-1.0 mm)' the size is 22.3 mm. A number or a slash pair written next to 'insulation', 'insulated', 'thick' or 'thickness' ('insulation : 13/19 mm', 'with 6/9 mm nitrile rubber insulation', '9 MM insulation foam') is a THICKNESS and is never the pipe size. Copy the words exactly as the BoQ writes them, as one continuous piece; never shorten, never join pieces with '...' or any other mark; if the words are long, copy the shortest continuous piece that holds the value.

attribute_definitions.label: Class / wall thickness
attribute_definitions.note: A class, wall thickness, schedule, grade or 'seamless' / 'ERW' the text states for the pipe, copied as written. A wall thickness written beside the size ('100NB - 5.4mm thick (Min)', 'wall Thickness-1.0 mm') is the PIPE's wall thickness: it goes here and is never an insulation thickness. Recorded and shown; it never changes the price (the sheet has one rate per size). Copy the words exactly as the BoQ writes them, as one continuous piece; never shorten, never join pieces with '...' or any other mark; if the words are long, copy the shortest continuous piece that holds the value.

attribute_definitions.label: Insulated
attribute_definitions.note: Whether THIS pipe is insulated. Yes when the row, or a heading that describes this row's pipe, says it is insulated or gives any insulation fact for it (a material, a thickness, 'duly insulated', 'with 9 MM insulation foam'). No only when the text says this pipe is NOT insulated (bare, uninsulated). Leave it out when the text does not mention insulation for this pipe. When Yes, also return the insulation as its own item in the insulation section, in the same position as its pipe.

'Touch Screen Central Controller' is a central / i-Touch / touch-panel controller for the whole system; 'BACnet Integration Controller for VRF Units' only when the row names BACnet or a BMS gateway. A drain pump bought on its own row is 'Drain Pump'. 'None' when the row does not say what kind of unit it is (an indoor unit whose type is not stated - a person picks it); 'none of these' when the row names an item that is not listed. VRF-5: an accessory the BoQ says is part of a unit's price (frame / stand, gas charge, drain pump, remote, refnet / Y-joint, MCCB / isolator, AV pads and the like) is answered on the unit item (its includes_* questions), never listed as a separate item, unless the row itself is that item. A central controller described as BACnet / BMS compatible is the 'Touch Screen Central Controller' (the BACnet item only when the row itself is a BACnet integration item). A ducted / ceiling suspended ducted indoor unit is 'Ductable'. An inclusion stated in a heading applies to every unit row under it. VRF-6: a frame / stand quoted per Nos is 'MS frame / stand for ODU' (per Kg it stays 'MS Angle Base Frame Structure'). A cassette the BoQ sizes as 600 x 600 mm or 2' x 2' is a Cassette (its way FOUR-WAY COMPACT). A CSU / ceiling suspended unit is 'Ductable'. An ON/OFF central controller is the 'Touch Screen Central Controller'. A capacity written with a stray space ('6 .3 TR') is that number (6.3 TR). Cabling the BoQ ties to a drain pump (a plug top, a power point for the pump) is the pump's, not the unit's power cable. VRF-7: a treated fresh air unit (TFA / fresh air unit) is 'Single Skin Treated Fresh Air', even when the BoQ also calls it CSU or ceiling suspended.

attribute_definitions.label: Includes copper piping
attribute_definitions.note: Yes when this row's text, or a heading that describes this unit, says the unit's price includes its refrigerant copper piping ('complete with copper piping', 'including refrigerant piping'). No when it says the copper is extra or by others. 'None' when it is silent. VRF-7: interconnecting piping named in a unit's heading or note is the copper piping stated: Yes. VRF-8: REQUIRED on every item - never leave it out. Answer Yes or No from the words wherever anything describes this unit's price or scope for it (decide - never leave it out because it is hard to tell); 'None' only when nothing at all describes it. With Yes, the _words answer copies ONE exact clause of the BoQ (never '...') and _where says where it sits. VRF-8: 'necessary interconnections with power supply / refrigerant connections' is connection work only, not the copper piping: No.

attribute_definitions.label: Includes insulation
attribute_definitions.note: Yes when the price includes insulation of the refrigerant piping it includes. No when it says insulation is extra or by others. 'None' when it is silent. VRF-7: suction line insulation named in a unit's heading or note is the insulation stated: Yes. VRF-8: REQUIRED on every item - never leave it out. Answer Yes or No from the words wherever anything describes this unit's price or scope for it (decide - never leave it out because it is hard to tell); 'None' only when nothing at all describes it. attribute_definitions.label: Includes power cable
attribute_definitions.note: Yes when the unit's price includes its power cabling / power supply wiring to the unit. No when it says it is extra or by others. 'None' when it is silent. Cabling for a drain pump (a plug top, a power point for the pump) is NOT the unit's power cable. VRF-8: REQUIRED on every item - never leave it out. Answer Yes or No from the words wherever anything describes this unit's price or scope for it (decide - never leave it out because it is hard to tell); 'None' only when nothing at all describes it. With Yes, the _words answer copies ONE exact clause of the BoQ (never '...') and _where says where it sits. VRF-8: 'inclusive of plug top & necessary power cable' on a unit is its power cable: Yes; cabling 'for the drain pump' is not. 'Necessary interconnections with power supply / earthing / refrigerant connections' is connection work only: No.

attribute_definitions.label: Includes communication cable
attribute_definitions.note: Yes when the unit's price includes its control / communication / transmission cabling. No when it says it is extra or by others. 'None' when it is silent. VRF-7: decide from the BoQ's words at EVERY level above the row (the row, its heading, the heading above that, the sheet's notes) whether the control / communication cabling is in this unit's scope. A sentence about how the system must behave when the control wiring fails or breaks down is NOT scope. A heading or note at any level that puts the control wiring in the scope IS scope. VRF-8: REQUIRED on every item - never leave it out. Answer Yes or No from the words wherever anything describes this unit's price or scope for it (decide - never leave it out because it is hard to tell); 'None' only when nothing at all describes it. With Yes, the _words answer copies ONE exact clause of the BoQ (never '...') and _where says where it sits.
